subject: Edison Labs: committed ARR gap from pending concession — pricing clearance needed
messages:
From: Maya Patel <maya.patel@edisonlabs.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: sales@edisonlabs.com, procurement@edisonlabs.com
Date: Mon, 02 Aug 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood proposal — procurement needs concession note

Hannah,

Thanks again for the walkthrough on Friday. Procurement reviewed the SOW and is asking for a one-time concession: a 15% list discount on the first-year committed seats to align internal budget cycles. We understand this is out of standard pricing and wanted to surface it early — Edison is ready to sign as soon as we get an OK.

Quick context: the total first-year ARR with the requested concession moves from $480k to ~$408k (annualized). They are pushing for a Q3 commitment.

I've attached the SOW and a short pricing table. Can you confirm who to loop in for approvals and expected turn time?

Attachments: Edison_SOW_v2.pdf (pdf), pricing_breakdown.xlsx (spreadsheet)

—Maya
Senior Procurement Manager
Edison Labs

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Aug 2027 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Redwood proposal — procurement needs concession note

Ben/Vanessa/Karthik — forwarding Edison request. Procurement is asking for a 15% first-year discount which creates a ~$72k delta to committed ARR if approved. They want a Q3 signature.

Impact: if we approve, Q3 committed ARR drops vs forecast; if we deny, deal risks slipping or losing to a competitor. Need quick deal-desk pricing guidance + explicit finance call on whether we can absorb this in the quarter or mark as uncommitted until formal approval.

Please reply with: 1) recommended concession (if any) and guardrails, 2) expected approval timeline, and 3) whether Finance should treat this as committed for forecast.

I've included the SOW and pricing table from Edison.

Thanks,
Hannah
Sr. Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Aug 2027 08:52:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood proposal — procurement needs concession note

Hannah — thanks for flagging. Quick read: a 15% one-time on year-one is material. My inclination: offer a structured concession rather than a flat list cut. Options to consider:

- Option A (preferred): 10% one-time on year-one + a 6-month ramp (50% discount on month 1-2 to soften commitment) — preserves ARR cadence and creates renewal hooks.
- Option B: 12% one-time if Edison commits to a 24-month term and a NBD payment cadence.
- Option C: deny and escalate (only if we have credible competitive intel).

To approve any concession >10% we need Deal Desk sign-off + Finance written agreement on how to treat the impact for this quarter's committed ARR. Vanessa/Karthik: can Deal Desk/Finance provide an approval time estimate? I've attached a quick pricing worksheet with modeled ARR impact and recovery scenarios.

Attachment: pricing_breakdown.xlsx (sheet with scenario tab)

Ben Carter
Director, Deal Desk

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Aug 2027 10:11:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood proposal — procurement needs concession note

Looping Finance (Karthik) — Ben's framing is good. From Deal Desk POV: we can fast-track up to 10% with a scoped approval if AE confirms no other discounts stacked (SOW services add-ons, credits, or pre-paid promotional items). Approvals >10% need Director sign-off + Finance co-sign. ETA on an answer: 24–36 hours if we get the signed commercial terms and a confirmed billing schedule.

Karthik — please confirm how you want this handled on the forecast while we await final approval. If Finance marks as committed today, we need a signed amendment before EoQ to avoid restatement risk. If you prefer to leave as pending, tell Hannah and we'll put a firm expiration on the concession.

Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Manager, Deal Operations

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 04 Aug 2027 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood proposal — procurement needs concession note

Thanks all — quick decision tree and next steps: 

1) Forecast treatment: do NOT count the concession-adjusted number as committed for Q3 until we have a fully executed amendment (signed SOW or P.O.). Treat current HubSpot committed ARR as-is (pre-concession) for the forecast. We will add a flagged line item under "At-Risk Adjustments" with the modeled delta so FP&A can see exposure.

2) Approval threshold: Deal Desk may approve up to 10% immediately with AE confirmation of no other concessions. >10% requires Director sign-off and Finance co-sign.

3) Recommended path for Hannah: propose Option A (10% + ramp) to Edison with a 72-hour approval window. Add a clause: concession expires if amendment not signed within 14 days. That buys us time and sets clear expectations.

I've updated the HubSpot deal record and attached the forecast snapshot. Finance will treat the potential delta as "at-risk" until legal/executed. If Deal Desk signs >10% and Finance co-signs, FP&A will reclassify the ARR in the next daily forecast run and notify Revenue Ops.

Attachment: commit_snapshot_2027-08.png (screenshot of HubSpot commit summary)

Karthik Iyer
Director, Revenue Finance
Redwood Inference

From: Maya Patel <maya.patel@edisonlabs.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 04 Aug 2027 17:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood proposal — procurement needs concession note

Hannah — thank you. Edison is happy to accept Option A (10% one-time + 6-month ramp) and will push for a 10-day signature window. Procurement prefers a 10-day window but agreed to 14 if needed. We will route the amendment to you by end of day tomorrow.

We appreciate the clarity on treatment for the forecast.

—Maya
